alternatives.reason_rejected: retrieval wants to show narrower records for a broad query; authority must never let a narrow record govern a broad scope

context: Wrote the v3 foundation ADR (docs/adr/2026-09-foundation-contracts.md, PROPOSED) and executable contracts in src/contracts (event envelope, canonical digest, ids, evidence classes, scope algebra, lifecycle payloads, delivery states, Ed25519 signing, ingress validation); 21 contract tests green, tsc clean.
rationale: The 2.x scopeMatches is bidirectional prefix on raw strings (src/auth matches src/authz) and is used for both retrieval and, implicitly, authority. C09 needs a narrow correction that never widens; C01 needs a review bound to its range; R13 needs repo identity as a hard filter that similar paths cannot cross.
summary: Two scope operations, deliberately distinct: scopeMatches (retrieval; bidirectional on path at segment boundaries, exact on tenant/repo/task/attempt/consumer, global events match any repo) and scopeGoverns (authority; unidirectional, a rule must name a repo or be global, revision-bound rules govern only their exact head)
